area: Git and workspaces: /Users/nkov47/IDE/workbench/src/core/workspace.mjs, src/core/receipt.mjs and test/workspace.test.mjs, and how diff, commit, land and discard can be built on the installed git 2.54.0 (Apple Git-157)
summary: workspace.mjs is the only module that runs git. Every call goes through git(args, { cwd, timeout = 30 s, input, okCodes }), which runs execFile('git', ['-c', 'core.fsmonitor=false', ...args]) with maxBuffer 64 MB and utf8. Its env is process.env without GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_NAMESPACE and GIT_PREFIX, plus GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, GIT_PAGER=cat and LC_ALL=LANG=C. It resolves { stdout, stderr } with no exit code, even when okCodes let a non-zero exit through. It rejects with the execFile error plus .stdout and .stderr. Errors a person sees are plainError(sentence, cause), with git's own words only in .detail. gitTrouble() words ENOENT ('Git is not installed, or it is not on the PATH.') and a killed process ('Git took too long and was stopped.'), and firstLine() strips 'fatal: ' and 'error: '. prepareRepo(p) expands ~, then runs `rev-parse --show-toplevel` (realpath'd), `rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD^{commit}`, `symbolic-ref --short --quiet HEAD` (null means a detached HEAD) and `status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=normal`. It returns { root, name, head, branch, dirty }. createWorkspace({ repoRoot, agentId, slug, baseDir }) checks the id against /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,63}$/. It makes the folder <baseDir or ~/.workbench/worktrees>/<repoName>-<sha1(realRoot)[:8]>/<slug>-<id> on branch workbench/<slug>-<id>. It first notes whether that branch is new (`rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/<b>`, okCodes [1]), then runs `worktree add -b <branch> <path> HEAD` (120 s timeout). It records base = `rev-parse HEAD` in the new worktree, i.e. the main checkout's HEAD commit at launch. The person's branch name at launch is not recorded anywhere: run.workspace and history keep only { path, branch, base }. If git fails part-way, takeBack (`worktree remove --force`, `branch -D`) runs only when the branch was new. removeWorkspace acts only on folders that `git worktree list --porcelain` lists (compared by canonical path), never on the main folder, and deletes only workbench/ branches. With onlyIfUnchanged it removes a folder only when HEAD === base, `status --porcelain --ignored --untracked-files=all` is empty and `worktree remove` without --force succeeds; then it runs `update-ref -d refs/heads/<b> <base>`. Otherwise it runs `worktree remove --force`, then `branch -D` with any failure swallowed. diffStats({ path, base }) runs in the worktree. It takes tracked changes from `git diff --numstat -z --no-renames --no-ext-diff --no-textconv <base> --` (worktree vs base: committed, staged and unstaged). It takes untracked files from `ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z` and line-counts them with countLines (lstat; a symlink counts as 1 line; over 2 MB or past a 64 MB budget is 'large'; a NUL in the first 8000 bytes is 'binary'). It also lists files hidden by an ignore rule the agent added or changed (marked ignored: true), by re-judging `ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard --directory -z` with `check-ignore --no-index` against base's .gitignore blobs written to a scratch folder. readRepoConfig reads workbench.json only from a commit (`git show --no-textconv <ref>:workbench.json`). validRef() allows /^[A-Za-z0-9._/@^~{}+-]{1,200}$/ with no leading '-' and no '..'. receipt.mjs runs no git: it does rule globbing (checkRules) and runs the declared checks through /bin/sh -c in the worktree (scrubbed env, own process group, timeouts). In the engine: createWorkspace runs at launch (engine.mjs:1632), diffStats at every root turn end (585), and readRepoConfig(ref = workspace.base) at launch and on continue (1644, 1320). removeWorkspace with onlyIfUnchanged runs when a start fails and at shutdown (1688), and prepareRepo runs at start and every 15 s. Nothing diffs, commits, merges or discards today. ARCHITECTURE.md:103 says 'the page offers no merge' and kept folders stay, and Forget never touches folders. Agents cannot `git add`, `commit`, `merge` or `checkout` without the person's OK: the policy's safe git list is status, diff, log, show, rev-parse, ls-files, blame, grep, and branch without -d. So finished work is normally uncommitted files in the worktree. test/workspace.test.mjs passes 16/16 on git 2.54.0 with node 26.13.1.

keyFacts.fact: merge-tree errors. Without --merge-base, an unknown ref exits 1 (the same code as a conflict) with stdout empty and stderr 'merge-tree: no-such-branch - not something we can merge'. With --merge-base it exits 128 with 'fatal: could not parse as tree 'no-such-branch''; a bad --merge-base=deadbeef gives the same message. Unrelated histories exit 128 with 'fatal: refusing to merge unrelated histories'. So treat a result as a conflict only when exit === 1 AND stdout starts with a 40- or 64-hex object id. With --merge-base, trees work in place of commits: '<BASE>^{tree} <P1>^{tree} <AG>^{tree}' gave the same clean tree, exit 0.
keyFacts.where: git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only main no-such-branch (stdout/stderr captured separately)

keyFacts.fact: Recorded base vs git's own merge base. Setup: the agent ran 'git merge main' after the person's commit P1, and the person then changed the same line again (P2). With --merge-base=<recorded base> the result is exit 1 'CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in f.txt', a false conflict. Without --merge-base, git uses merge-base = P1: exit 0, and f.txt = 'l1 P2 l3', which is correct. So do not pass the recorded base to merge-tree for a real merge.

keyFacts.fact:
`git merge --ff-only --no-autostash <C>` in the person's main checkout, by dirty state:
- An unrelated unstaged or staged edit: exit 0, and the edit is kept (' M c.txt' / 'M  c.txt').
- An edit (unstaged or staged) to a file the landing changes: exit 1, stderr 'error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge:\n\ta.txt\nPlease commit your changes or stash them before you merge.\nAborting'. 'Updating 9a4d8bb..416e133' also appears; which stream it goes to was not checked. HEAD and the edit are unchanged.
- An untracked file at a path the agent adds: exit 1, 'error: The following untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge:\n\tnew.txt\nPlease move or remove them before you merge.\nAborting'.
- The person's branch has diverged: exit 128, hint lines then 'fatal: Not possible to fast-forward, aborting.'

- CHERRY_PICK_HEAD present: exit 128, 'fatal: You have not concluded your cherry-pick (CHERRY_PICK_HEAD exists).'
- Detached HEAD: exit 0, but only the detached HEAD moves and no branch gets the work.

Hooks:
- .git/hooks/post-merge runs on a fast-forward merge.
- '-c core.hooksPath=<empty dir>' stops it.
- A pre-commit hook runs on `git commit` and can block it (exit 1); the empty hooksPath stops it too.
- commit-tree never runs hooks.

keyFacts.fact: `update-ref -m land refs/heads/main <AG> <T0>` on the CHECKED-OUT branch exits 0. It moves HEAD but leaves the index and worktree alone, so status shows 'D  .env|M  a.txt|D  new.txt': a staged revert that the person's next commit would record. With a wrong old value it exits 128: 'fatal: update_ref failed for ref 'refs/heads/main': cannot lock ref 'refs/heads/main': is at <X> but expected <Y>'. `fetch . workbench/land-bbb222:main` while main is checked out exits 128: 'fatal: refusing to fetch into branch 'refs/heads/main' checked out at '/private/tmp/.../land''. Into a branch that is not checked out it exits 0 (fast-forward only).

Snapshot without touching the agent's index:
- Commands: `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp> git read-tree <HEAD>` (or a copy of `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index`), `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp> git add -A`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp> git write-tree`, then `git commit-tree <tree> -p <HEAD> -m ...`.
- Effect: the agent's index is unchanged (ls-files -s hash compared) and its status is unchanged.
- Contents: staged and unstaged edits, deletions and untracked files.
- A symlink to /tmp/.../outside.txt is stored as mode 120000 holding only the link text, never the target's content.
- Files hidden by an agent-written .gitignore (secret/x.sql) and node_modules/ are NOT included; `git add -f -- secret/x.sql` adds the hidden file.
- The same content gives the same tree id (23d8eba0... twice); one edit gives a new id.

A nested repository with no commits makes `git add -A` fail with exit 128: 'error: 'nest/' does not have a commit checked out\nerror: unable to index file 'nest/'\nfatal: adding files failed'. The temp index then holds only what read-tree put there, so `write-tree` returns the base tree and the snapshot looks like 'no changes' unless the add's exit code is checked. With --ignore-errors the add exits 1 and goes on. A nested repo WITH a commit is added as a gitlink, '160000 1bc12c92... 0\tnest2', with a long 'warning: adding embedded git repository: nest2' hint. `ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z` lists both as 'nest/' and 'nest2/' (trailing slash). The pathspecs `-- . ':(exclude,literal)nest/' ':(exclude,literal)nest2/'` work (exit 0).

Patch output:
- Command: `git -c core.quotePath=false -c core.bigFileThreshold=1k diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-color --no-renames --submodule=short --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/ <base> <snapshot>`, exit 0.
- A 3 KB text file prints 'Binary files /dev/null and b/big.txt differ', so bigFileThreshold works as a per-file cap. numstat then prints '-\t-\tbig.txt' (the default is '50\t0\tbig.txt'), indistinguishable from a real binary.
- A symlink prints 'new file mode 120000' and '+/tmp/.../outside.txt' with '\ No newline at end of file'.
- A deletion prints 'deleted file mode 100644'.

- `git diff --no-index -- /dev/null link-out` also shows only the link text and exits 1 when the files differ.

(no gpg output)

keyFacts.fact: Committing the agent's work on its own branch: `update-ref -m '...' refs/heads/workbench/snap-ddd444 <C> <oldHEAD>`, run from the main repo while the branch is checked out in the agent's worktree, exits 0. The agent's status is then stale: 'MM a.txt|D  big.txt|...|?? big.txt|...'. After `git -C <ws> reset -q` (mixed) the status is empty, and ignored files (node_modules/, secret/) are untouched.

Discard primitives:
- `branch -D` while the branch's worktree exists exits 1: 'error: cannot delete branch 'workbench/disc-eee555' used by worktree at '/private/tmp/.../disc-agent''.
- `update-ref -d <ref> <wrong old>` exits 1 (not 128): 'error: cannot lock ref '...': is at <X> but expected <Y>'.
- Unforced `worktree remove` on a dirty folder exits 128: 'fatal: '<path>' contains modified or untracked files, use --force to delete it'.
- A locked worktree with a single --force exits 128: 'fatal: cannot remove a locked working tree, lock reason: testing\nuse 'remove -f -f' to override or unlock first'. `--force --force` exits 0.
- After the branch is deleted its commit appears only in 'git fsck --unreachable' until gc prunes it (default about 2 weeks). Uncommitted files deleted by --force have no git object at all.
`git replay --ref-action=print --onto main <HEAD>..<branch>` prints 'update refs/heads/workbench/snap-ddd444 <new> <old>\n', exit 0. It is experimental.

On Node 26, an execFile maxBuffer overflow gives err.code 'ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER' (RangeError 'stdout maxBuffer length exceeded'), with err.killed and err.signal undefined. gitTrouble() therefore returns null, and callers build sentences like 'Git could not compare the workspace with its starting point: ' with an empty firstLine. A whole-tree diff can pass the 64 MB MAX_BUFFER.

git() returns { stdout, stderr } and never the exit code, so okCodes cannot tell merge-tree's 0 from its 1; read err.code and err.stdout from the rejection, or change the helper. gitEnv() deletes GIT_INDEX_FILE and git() takes no env option, so a temp-index snapshot needs a helper change, for example an indexFile option set after gitEnv().
diffStats silently compares with HEAD when base is missing: `validRef(base || 'HEAD')`.

removeWorkspace's force path swallows a failed `branch -D` but still returns { removed: true, branch }. The onlyIfUnchanged path swallows a failed `update-ref -d`. A single --force throws on a locked worktree: 'Git could not remove the workspace: cannot remove a locked working tree, ...'.

base is set by `rev-parse HEAD` inside the new worktree (workspace.mjs:212). History keeps workspace as { path, branch, base }, but cleanWorkspace only clips branch and base to 200 characters. A base read back from the history file is never validated, so run validRef or an OID check before any git use.

base has two jobs: it is the diff origin (engine.mjs:585) and the trusted ref that workbench.json is read from (_loadConfig at engine.mjs:1720-1732), both at launch (1644) and when an earlier agent continues (1320). Moving base forward after a landing would make the agent's own workbench.json edits (checks, allow prefixes) trusted.

repoInfo, which prepareRepo refreshes every repoEveryMs = 15 s, can be up to 15 s stale. snapshot().repo is { name, head, branch, dirty }. Landing must call prepareRepo again and bind to the head and branch the confirm card showed.

Earlier agents (restored from history) have no run, only earlierRecs.get(id). _historyRecords writes that record back unchanged (1265-1281). _canContinue checks rec.workspace.path for a directory with a .git entry. A discard or landing on an earlier agent must update rec.workspace itself (null after removal) and call store.markContinue (store.mjs:434).
There are two slugify functions. The engine's own (32 characters) runs before createWorkspace's (40 characters).

The dogfood repo:
- git top level is /Users/nkov47/IDE (the code is in workbench/); the checkout is on branch cloud-build, clean, with only branches cloud-build and main.
- There is no workbench.json at /Users/nkov47/IDE.
- No user.name or user.email is set in any config, and there is no ~/.gitconfig; only the system config's init.defaultbranch.
- .git/hooks holds only samples.

- VS Code's git integration is in use (branch.*.vscode-merge-base keys).

The Claude runner starts Claude Code with --input-format stream-json, so a done Claude agent's process probably stays alive between turns (not verified). Shutdown tidies only runs whose runner reports alive !== true. Codex exits after every turn.

The done lid already has its two buttons, 'Looks good' (primary) and 'Ask for a change'. 'What changed?' is a quiet link shown only in the 'more' detail level; it lists the first 6 files from view.files.

Engine tests fake the whole workspace module in test/helpers/engine-fakes.mjs (prepareRepo, createWorkspace, diffStats, readRepoConfig, removeWorkspace), each recording its calls in calls.<fn>. Any new function needs a fake there.

test/workspace.test.mjs passes 16/16 on git 2.54.0 with node v26.13.1 in about 2.5 s. It isolates git with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 and author/committer env vars, a mkdtemp folder and baseDir. Its last test asserts that nothing was written to ~/.workbench.

extensionPoints.capability: (shared) git() helper changes that every new capability needs
extensionPoints.how:
1. Add an optional indexFile parameter that sets env.GIT_INDEX_FILE after gitEnv() has deleted it. Use an absolute path inside an fs.mkdtempSync(os.tmpdir()/'workbench-index-') folder, removed in finally, as ignoredAt does with its scratch folder (321-363).
2. Add a way to get the exit code. Either resolve { stdout, stderr, code } or catch the rejection and read err.code and err.stdout.
3. Map ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER in gitTrouble to a plain sentence, or avoid relying on MAX_BUFFER (see the diff entry).
4. Keep GIT_SAFE_CONFIG. For commands run in the person's main checkout, also pass '-c core.hooksPath=<empty temp dir>' (verified to stop post-merge and pre-commit hooks), or make that a deliberate decision (see openQuestions).

extensionPoints.capability: Snapshot of an agent's work as git objects (the basis for the diff, the commit, landing and discard binding)
extensionPoints.how:
Signature, for example: snapshotWork({ repoRoot, path }) -> { head, tree, commit, left: [paths not included] }. 1. realRoot(repoRoot). The folder must be in listWorktrees(root) (235-244), as removeWorkspace checks. Optionally check that `git -C ws rev-parse --git-common-dir` resolves to root's common dir. 2. head = `rev-parse --verify HEAD^{commit}` in ws. 3. Temp index: copy the agent's index file (`rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index`) or run `read-tree `. The copy keeps files the agent staged with -f and the stat cache. 4. Nested repos: list entries ending in '/' from `ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z` and exclude each with ':(exclude,literal)

'. 5. Run `add -A -- . ` and CHECK the exit code: a failed add makes write-tree return the base tree. 6. If the receipt's ignored: true files must be covered, run `add -f -- ` in batches of ARG_BATCH (500). 7. Run `write-tree`, then `commit-tree -p -m `. 8. Before hashing, refuse or ask about untracked files over COUNT_FILE_MAX_BYTES; diffStats' large flag already marks them. 9. If the snapshot must outlive gc or a restart, keep it under refs/workbench/snapshots/ (not shown by `git branch`) and delete that ref on land, discard and forget. Tests: in test/workspace.test.mjs, reuse the fixture from 'createWorkspace makes a worktree...' (131-219) and the hidingWorkspace helper (276-286). Assert that the agent's `ls-files -s` is unchanged, that an outside symlink is stored as mode 120000 with only its link text, that a commit-less nested repo is reported rather than silently dropped, and that the same content gives the same tree id.

extensionPoints.capability: (a) Full textual diff of an agent's worktree vs its base, untracked files included
extensionPoints.where: new export in workspace.mjs, e.g. diffPatch({ path, base, maxFileBytes, maxTotalBytes }); engine method plus a route such as GET /api/agents/:id/diff
extensionPoints.how:
1. Require base (validRef; do not default to HEAD as diffStats does at 408).
2. Snapshot as above, so untracked files, deletions and staged and unstaged edits all come from one tree.
3. List: `diff --name-status -z --no-renames <base> <snap>` and `--numstat -z`.
4. Patches: `git -c core.quotePath=false -c core.bigFileThreshold=<cap, e.g. 512k> diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-color --no-renames --submodule=short --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/ <base> <snap> -- ':(literal)<path>'`. Run it per file or in batches, cut each patch to maxFileBytes and stop at maxTotalBytes.
5. Tell large from binary by size (`ls-tree -l` or `cat-file -s`), because bigFileThreshold makes numstat print '-\t-' for both.
6. Symlinks show only their link text, so content outside the folder never reaches the page.
7. Return { tree, base, files: [{ path, status, adds, dels, binary?, large?, cut?, patch }] }. The tree id is the binding token for a later land or discard.
8. Add a fake in test/helpers/engine-fakes.mjs, guard in the engine with typeof this.deps.workspace?.diffPatch === 'function', and escape everything with esc() in the UI.
9. Document it in ARCHITECTURE.md's 'Workspaces and receipt' section (379-403) and the HTTP table.

extensionPoints.capability: (b) Commit the agent's uncommitted work in its worktree as the person
extensionPoints.where: new export in workspace.mjs, e.g. commitWork({ repoRoot, path, expectTree, message })
extensionPoints.how:
1. Snapshot, and require tree === expectTree (bound to what the person saw).
2. Make the commit with commit-tree, never `git commit` in the worktree: commit-tree runs no hooks and ignores commit.gpgSign (verified). Add -S explicitly only if signing is wanted.
3. Move the branch with `update-ref -m 'workbench: ...' refs/heads/<branch> <C> <head>`, a compare-and-swap that refuses if the agent committed meanwhile. The branch must be the worktree's `symbolic-ref HEAD` and start with workbench/.
4. Run `git -C ws reset -q` (mixed) so the agent's index matches. Verified: status is empty afterwards and ignored files are untouched.
5. Before committing, check identity with `git config user.name` and `git config user.email`. When they are unset, git silently uses an auto-detected identity (verified), which is the case on the dogfood machine.
6. Decide whether the diff base advances to C. It must not change the config ref (see rulesToHonour).

extensionPoints.capability: (c) Land the work in the person's current branch in the MAIN checkout, never touching their uncommitted edits
extensionPoints.where: new export in workspace.mjs, e.g. landWork({ repoRoot, path, base, expect: { branch, head, tree }, message, squash }), plus a confirm flow in the engine
extensionPoints.how:
1. info = prepareRepo(root), fresh (repoInfo can be 15 s old). Refuse when info.branch is null: a detached HEAD fast-forwards onto no branch (verified). Refuse when info.branch !== expect.branch or info.head !== expect.head ('That changed. Have another look.'). 2. Refuse while an operation is in progress: `rev-parse --git-path` for MERGE_HEAD, CHERRY_PICK_HEAD, REVERT_HEAD, rebase-merge, rebase-apply and BISECT_LOG. merge itself refuses MERGE_HEAD and CHERRY_PICK_HEAD with exit 128 (verified); REVERT_HEAD is untested. 3. Snapshot again and require tree === expect.tree. 4. Ancestry guard: `merge-base --is-ancestor

` (exit 0 or 1). If base is not an ancestor, refuse or fall back to squash; a merge would otherwise pull in commits from a branch the person left. Untested. 5. rulesToHonour: Every git call goes through git() in workspace.mjs: execFile with an argument array, a timeout, GIT_SAFE_CONFIG (core.fsmonitor=false) and gitEnv() (no GIT_DIR, GIT_INDEX_FILE and the other redirect variables; no prompts, no optional locks, C locale). Never use a shell string. Pass paths with '--' and ':(literal)' or --literal-pathspecs, and refs through validRef(), full 'refs/heads/...' names or 40/64-hex object ids.

Config is read only from a commit, never from the agent's working copy (readRepoConfig at workspace.mjs:490-514; engine _loadConfig reads from workspace.base). Keep the trusted config ref separate from any diff base that moves after a landing. Surface landed changes to workbench.json, .claude/** and .mcp.json, because they become trusted for every later agent launched from the person's HEAD.

Plain language: errors are plainError(sentence) with git's words only in .detail. Sentences, not identifiers; use src/shared/narrate.mjs. Build conflict and 'in the way' sentences from file paths, not from git's message text.

Confirm cards: anything destructive or that changes the person's checkout must go through command() and a confirm card { id, sentence, detail }, then confirm(id, go). Cards expire after 10 min and are settled only by the confirmId on screen. Cancel replies follow 'OK, I won’t …'. Forget is the model to copy: _proposeForget and _forgetEarlier at engine.mjs:1370-1400.

Answer binding: act only on what the person saw, by id. For landing or discarding, bind to the snapshot tree id and the person's branch and HEAD shown on the card, and refuse if any changed ('That changed. Have another look.'). Refusals are { ok: false, reply } with status 200.
The lid shows one thing at a time with at most two answers. The done lid already uses 'Looks good' and 'Ask for a change'.

Kept-work rule (ARCHITECTURE.md:103): the worktree and its workbench/ branch are the only copy of the work. Nothing that might hold work is removed without an explicit, bound confirm. The onlyIfUnchanged semantics of shutdown and failed-start tidying must not change.
removeWorkspace invariants: never the main folder; only folders that `git worktree list` lists; only workbench/ branches; the worktree is removed before the branch.

Fast-forward only in the main checkout: the person's checkout only ever sees `merge --ff-only --no-autostash --no-overwrite-ignore` to a commit built elsewhere (merge-tree and commit-tree in the object database). Never a real merge, never update-ref on a checked-out branch, never conflict markers.

History records are built field by field (recordOf and cleanRecord); no command output, tokens or environment. Writes are atomic. New fields are cleaned again on load, and the folder becomes null when it is removed.
